newsitem.title: DUBAI: Cold snap and rain worsen Kurdish refugees' plight.
newsitem.headline: Cold snap and rain worsen Kurdish refugees' plight.

text.p: A sharp drop in temperature and heavy rain have worsened the plight of tens of thousands of Kurdish refugees who fled Iraq to Iran, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported late on Wednesday.
"Heavy rainfall over the past 24 hours and fall of temperatures by 15 degrees have made relief operations difficult for the Iraqi Kurdish refugees," IRNA said.
It said the refugees lacked "proper heating equipment and warm clothing."
It quoted Iranian Red Crescent official, Seyyed Qasem Hassanzadeh, as saying available supplies were only enough to cater for the refugees for one month.

"Meanwhile, the Kurdish refugees have become resentful of the indifference of international bodies to their problem. They said if international relief aid is not forthcoming, the refugees would be exposed to death," IRNA added.

Iran, which said in late September it was sheltering 65,000 refugees, has repeatedly said the refugees faced bleak winter conditions at their mountain camps and held the international community responsible for their plight.
The refugees fled to Iran from northern Iraq after its takeover by the Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) in September.
Iran said on Monday some have been returning across the border after the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) retook some territory from the KDP.
Iran's Marivan city governor Ali Yari said about 1,000 refugees had already left and more were expected to follow.
